After months of headaches, countless trips to the bike store, home depot, and the bank, the stupid !@#$!@#$ bike is complete....for now.

TL:DR - Lots of work, small parts, and custom work required but it runs great. Cant wait to do another one!

Parts List - I will try to be as complete as possible.

Frame: GT2-A Skyhawk

Engine: Flying Horse 66/80cc kit from BikeBerry.com.

Engine Upgrades: 0.66mm NT carb jet, NGK BP7HS spark plug, heavy duty high performance air filter, Sick Bike Parts expansion chamber, kill rocker switch, performance throttle, heavy duty fuel valve, high compression head, reed valve kit (not pictured),

Bike Parts: v-brake calipers, kool-stop brake bads, dual brake handle, heavy duty 12 gauge 26x2.125 rims, 36 tooth sprocket, 415 heavy duty chain, 2" bottom bracket cups and parts, 1-piece pedal crank, 32 tooth chain ring, white bicycle chain, pedals, 31.8mm seat clamp, 1" lay back seat post, seat (borrowed from cruiser), XLC white cable hosing, black ops white brake cable, grease, CST Cyclops pro 26x2.4 tires, 1 1/8" suspension forks, headset stem, handlebars..whew!

I get long winded so I apologize in advance but I want to make this as helpful as possible. I've had to go to so many different sites to learn about all the possible problems and fixes out there. So here goes the build story...

Putting bike parts together

It seems there are special tools required to put the bottom bracket on and headset pieces. I just used a piece of wood and hammer to wack the cups into place. A few good hits and everything pops on. I was given a fork so I had to get creative fitting the headset and stem on. I left out the biggest piece the headset came with and used a smaller "washer" to get the fit just right. If you buy a new fork you will have to cut it down to size. Not complicated so if you have a question on how to do this let me know. The stock headset that came with the frame is working fine. Just make sure all these parts get lubbed up.

Engine Work Done

Matched the intake and exhaust ports. Used a dremel to make the ports on the cylinder body larger. Sanded down the head to lessen the gap between the top of the piston (increases compression).

Problems Encountered

Frame had the rear dropouts bent. Not major but check your frame! Another Redditor had the whole back side bent. The frame came with a headset but no instructions. Look online for how to put together a Cane Creek 40 headset and its the same. The rear engine mount was too big. I had to cut it with a coping saw to fit. Replaced the cheap bolts with hex bolts from Home Depot. Fuel filter doesnt fit well. Picture shows bike without one but I ended up getting different fuel line and getting it to fit. Just not a lot of space here. My "high performance" air filter does not fit so picture has stock filter. Seat post is not wide enough, had to use a shim but its still moving around on me. Handlebars are too narrow as well and used a shim to fit. I am short so going with the layback seat makes me stretch far. The SBP pipe was a bitch to mount. Went to Home Depot and bought various copper fittings to try. Finally got it to work with one 90 degree and one 45 degree fitting. Still doesnt feel like its in all the way.

Work still needed

Exhaust bolt stripped!!! Its actually on the body so I have to replace the entire cylinder body! FUCK. Need to add the kill switch. Right now I'm stopping, holding the brake in, and releasing the clutch to kill it. V-brakes dont work well. Plan to get new rim that takes disc brakes. Add reed valve kit? I bought it from Arrow Motors and its so out of spec. They refused to exchange because I took too long to mention it. FUCK. Gas leaks from valve and bicycle chain is too long. Removing a link is too short.

What about disc brakes?

Ok...if you want to get disc brakes I feel you need to know what parts you need. Its not as easy as they make it sound.

For front: Rims that accept disc brakes, rotor (recommend 185mm), Avid BB7 brake, and cable.

For rear: This gets tricky due to lack of space. Rear disc brake hub, sprocket adapter, rotor, brake caliper, caliper mount (there is one for the Skyhawk frame) plus the actual wheel/rim. Scroll to bottom of Jake Bike's page for more info.
